title: Change the toner cartridge in a desktop laser printer and close its front door
instruction: Put the new toner cartridge in the printer in place of the used one, leave the used one on the table, and close the printer.
context: Changing the toner in a laser printer is routine upkeep in most offices and many homes. The used cartridge has to come out of its bay, the new one has to go in square between the side guides all the way to the back stop, and the front door will not shut over a cartridge left standing out. A cartridge that is dropped or tipped over can spill toner.
setup: Station table. Positions in cm: x forward from the line between the arm bases, y to the robot's left from their midpoint, heights above the table. Printer: a desktop mono laser printer the size of an HP LaserJet Pro M404n (38.1 wide, 35.7 deep, 21.6 tall), light grey ABS, standing square to the robot with its front face at x 24, centred on y 0; it is modelled fixed (8.2 kg on rubber feet). The paper cassette fills the bottom 3.5 cm of its front; on top are a dark output tray, a control panel at the front right and the door release button at the front left. Toner bay: behind the front door, 34 wide between its side walls (the guides), 10.8 deep from the front face to its back stop, floor 3.5 above the table, walls to the full height. Front door: L-shaped grey ABS, 350 g, 34.8 wide, 1.2 thick: a front panel 18.1 tall and a top lip 10.8 deep (shut, the lip is the front of the printer's top, over the bay). It is hinged along the bay floor's front edge and turns 90 degrees from shut to flat open. It starts fully open: the panel lies flat toward the robot (x 5.9 to 24) with its inner face level with the bay floor, and the lip stands up at its end (x 5.9 to 7.1, top 14.3 high). Its weight is behind the hinge when shut, so it falls shut within about 7 degrees of shut and falls open beyond that; a catch holds it once it is within 1.5 degrees of shut. Shut, its inside is 6 mm in front of a seated cartridge. Toner cartridges (two, the same shape, standing in for HP 58A cartridges): a black moulded body 33 long (along y), 10 deep, 8.5 tall, 0.65 kg, with grey 0.8 cm end caps, a white label on the front and a green shutter strip along the top back; a carry handle along the top of the front: a bar 16 long, 1.4 thick, 2 tall, centred 3 behind the front face, on two 1.5 wide posts at its ends, with a 1.5 finger gap under it (bar top 12 above the cartridge's bottom). The used cartridge (grey handle) starts seated: body centred at (29.6, 0), bottom on the bay floor, its back 2 mm from the stop. The new cartridge (orange handle) stands upright on the table to the right of the printer, square to it, body centred at (19, -39). The table to the left of the printer is clear. Nothing else is on the table; the arms start at their ready pose.
scoring: Judged from the video and a final photo, with a tape measure. 0 for the whole trial if at any moment a cartridge is dropped (falls faster than 0.5 m/s, about 1.3 cm of free fall), tips more than 30 degrees from upright, or leaves the table. Otherwise, at the end: 0.25 if the used cartridge is out of the printer, resting on the table (its lowest point within 5 mm of it, level within 5 degrees), with no part over the printer's footprint or the open door's footprint, and no hand within 5 mm of it. 0.5 if, as well, the new cartridge is seated: its body within 4 mm of the seated position along and across the bay, its bottom within 3 mm of the bay floor, square and level within 3 degrees, and no hand within 5 mm of it. 0.75 if, as well, the door is shut and caught (it reached within 1.5 degrees of shut and is now within 2 degrees of shut). 1.0 if, as well, no hand is within 5 mm of either cartridge or the door, and neither cartridge nor the door has moved for 1 s. Doing nothing scores 0.
reset_notes: 1. Unplug the printer and check it stands on its taped outline. 2. Take the new (orange-tape) cartridge out and stand it upright on its taped mark to the right of the printer, square to it. 3. Slide the used (grey) cartridge into the bay along the guides until it stops, so it sits flat on the bay floor. 4. Press the door release and let the door fall open flat. Both cartridges are spent HP 58A cartridges (empty ones returned for recycling); tape over each one's drum opening so its residual toner stays inside, and wrap the new one's handle in orange tape.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 240 Hz physics, 20 Hz control. The printer is fixed; its door is a hinged link with stops at shut and flat open and a catch (a stiff hold switched on within 1.5 degrees of shut). Bay, guides, door and cartridges are boxes at the stated sizes with 5 mm play per end; the cartridge's rounded top and label are visual only. ABS friction 0.35. No electronics, chip contacts or toner.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (mean of 2 trials); demo: 1.0 (2 trials, 1.0 each)
